I just said, ‘look, I cannot call him, the guy is responsible for the death of my mother’.” ; “Yes, he asked me to call Zoe Pennue because he wanted to make peace... When I explained my position to him, the thing I liked about him was that he understood. He said, ‘oh, it's deeper problem’... But then, these elders who have been through a lot of the meetings, seemed not to understand.” ; Further disclosed that the Boakai-led government is doing everything possible to ensure a decent, state funeral for her parents, and that she is excited how President Boakai has personally engaged the family during this sad period of their bereavement, disclosing that the Liberian leader even made a personal contribution toward the funeral proceedings.

a6710.speaker: Participants at the GIZ-hosted panel discussion in Juba
a6710.speech: Recommended that survivors of GBV in South Sudan are significantly in need of assistance and safeguarding; discussed challenges faced by survivors of GBV, the role of the judiciary in providing justice and protection as well as community and cultural dynamics in addressing GBV.

a6710.speaker: Survivors of sexualised and gender-based violence (statements read to the audience)
a6710.speech: Statements of survivors were read to the audience during the powerful opening remarks.

a6710.speaker: Lea Flaspoehler, Cluster Coordinator for Governance and Gender, GIZ South Sudan
a6710.speech: "While focusing on prevention, we also pay special attention to the needs of survivors of SGBV. For example, we support the One Stop Centre in Yei, where survivors can receive holistic care."

a6710.speaker: Alice Oleya Jino, Program Manager at the European Union
a6710.speech: "Gender equality and human rights are core values, mainstreamed in all European Union internal and external policies. We are fully committed to the gender agenda and to place women and gender equality at the heart of peace and security."

a6710.speaker: GIZ
a6710.speech: Pointed out that gender-based violence is a pervasive global issue that transcends geographical, cultural and social boundaries, adding survivors often face systemic barriers, stigma, and silence when seeking justice and protection ; "For women and girls in displacement situations, the risk of being affected is particularly high. The availability of services for the care of survivors, such as psycholgocial support, health services and legal advice, is limited and in some places non-existent."

a6761.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a6761.speech: Has pledged to improve working conditions for civil servants and ensure the timely payment of their salaries, acknowledging the difficult circumstances they continue to face ; reassured civil servants of the government's commitment to salary reform and pledged to implement sustainable measures that will strengthen the public service sector.

a6761.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a6761.speech: Praised the resilience and commitment of public workers, saying their perseverance in the face of economic hardship is both admirable and essential to the country's progress: "I extend my heartfelt appreciation to all the hardworking men and women of South Sudan. Your tireless efforts and unwavering dedication to the growth, development, and stability of our beloved nation."

a6761.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a6761.speech: Expressed gratitude to the diplomatic community, UN agencies, international organizations, and NGOs for their ongoing contributions to peacebuilding, humanitarian assistance, and national development: "Your continued support and cooperations to peacebuilding, humanitarian response, and national development are instrumental as we move forward in the spirit of partnership and mutual respect."

a6761.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a6761.speech: Encouraged citizens to use Labour Day as an opportunity for reflection on the country's journey so far and the shared responsibility to build a future marked by peace, economic growth, and social justice, concluding by calling for national unity guided by the principles of dignity, accountability, and collective responsibility.

a6988.speaker: José Maria Neves, President of the Republic of Cabo Verde
a6988.speech: Spoke about the main challenges facing Africa and Cabo Verde in his address to a High-Level Dialogue panel at the 16th US-Africa Business Summit in Dallas; in this regard he referred to the socioeconomic transformation process under way and the possibilities of partnerships with the Government of the United States, as well as with private companies.

a7015.speaker: Nnamdi Azikiwe, Nigerian nationalist leader and first president
a7015.speech: As Azikiwe once wrote, politics in Nigeria is ‘a means to an end which is more glorious than the means through which this end must be attained.’

a7015.speaker: Nnamdi Azikiwe, Nigerian nationalist leader (in his 1937 book Renascent Africa)
a7015.speech: Wrote about the necessity of birthing a ‘New Africa’ and a ‘New Nigeria’, whilst swearing off old habits that impeded social regeneration, mental emancipation, economic determinism and spiritual balance ; ‘There must be revolutionary changes in order to have a new order,’ wrote Azikiwe in 1937.

a7015.speaker: Peter Obi's presidential manifesto (Labour Party policy document)
a7015.speech: His promise of restructuring is laden with unrelieved vagueness—i.e. ‘moving agreed items to the concurrent list’—and an impractical faith in the federal legislature; contains references like ‘Marshall-plan type programme’, the ‘promotion of made-in-Nigeria goods’, his intention to marry unspecified aspects of ‘our customary laws’ with the country’s ‘formal law’, emphasis on the Oronsaye Report, and the creation of an ‘Office of Special Counsel to investigate and prosecute every executive abuse of power that do not fall under the prosecutorial power of existing agencies or are bureaucratically concealed’, plus a nebulous ‘Green Army’ concept.

a7015.speaker: Atiku Abubakar's presidential manifesto
a7015.speech: Atiku’s plan to besiege the country with neoliberal policies, with expertly worded neoliberal globalization language, including ‘liberalization of the foreign exchange market’, financialization and privatization of capital and factors of production, and promotion of made-in-Nigeria goods.

a7015.speaker: John Dramani Mahama's manifesto (Ghana)
a7015.speech: The social-democratic manifesto of John Dramani Mahama of Ghana is profoundly true to its ideological purpose, unambiguous in its apprehension of the problem and solutions, clear in its programmatic goals and resolute in its elaboration of retributive and restorative action.

a7233.speaker: Femi Babafemi, spokesperson of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) (statement)
a7233.speech: In a statement made available to Channels Television, the agency said the consignments were concealed in the private part, stomach, and false bottom of the handbag of the suspect, identified as Ihensekhien Miracle Obehi ; said that the suspect, who was dressed in a hijab to beat security checks, was intercepted at the departure hall of the Port Harcourt airport on Sunday, May 3, 2025, while trying to board a Qatar Airline flight to Iran via Doha, following credible intelligence ; disclosed that during a search on Obehi, she was found to have inserted three wraps of cocaine in her private part, and two large parcels hidden in false compartments of her handbag, while she swallowed 67 pellets of the Class A drug.

a7233.speaker: National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
a7233.speech: Said its operatives thwarted what it described as a desperate attempt by a woman to export large consignments of cocaine to Iran at the Port Harcourt International Airport in Rivers State; according to the NDLEA, the total weight of the three consignments hidden in different parts of her body comes to 2.523 kilograms.

a7233.speaker: Ihensekhien Miracle Obehi, suspect arrested by the NDLEA
a7233.speech: According to Babafemi, Obehi claimed she was to swallow 70 pellets of cocaine, but after ingesting 67 pieces, she could no longer swallow the remaining three and decided to insert them into her private part.

a7341.speaker: Communiqué of the 8th Nigeria Family Planning Conference, signed by Dr Ejike Oji
a7341.speech: Contained the outcomes of the conference, made available to newsmen on Thursday in Abuja: the conference secured a significant $4 million commitment from the private sector to support family planning programs until 2030; a pledge from the National Assembly to advocate for dedicated legislation on family planning funding; and recognition of the urgent need for inclusive, data-driven policy reforms to tackle demographic challenges.

a7341.speaker: Stakeholders at the 8th Nigeria Family Planning Conference (government officials, international partners, religious leaders, youth representatives)
a7341.speech: Called for urgent policy reforms, increased funding, and stronger advocacy to achieve Nigeria's Family Planning 2030 (FP2030) goals; identified pressing challenges hindering the country's progress, including irregular census and poor data collection systems; funding shortages, especially in research and family planning commodity supply chains; cultural and religious resistance to modern contraceptive methods; insufficient male involvement in family planning advocacy; and weak integration of family planning into Nigeria's health policies.

a7341.speaker: Participants at the 8th Nigeria Family Planning Conference
a7341.speech: Resolved that faith-based and traditional leaders should intensify advocacy for family planning within their communities; government at all levels should establish dedicated budget lines for family planning and ensure timely release of funds; religious and community leaders should promote modern contraceptive methods and dispel myths; efforts should be increased to integrate family planning into national development strategies, including the Sector-Wide Approach (SWAp); health facilities should be strengthened with trained personnel and improved access, especially in rural areas; youth-focused sexual and reproductive health education should be expanded; the Federal Ministry of Education should integrate family planning education into the school curriculum at all levels; and stronger interfaith collaboration is needed to break religious and cultural barriers to contraceptive use. They emphasised that all stakeholders must act on these resolutions by 2027 to ensure equitable and sustainable family planning services across Nigeria.

a7341.speaker: Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, CON, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives
a7341.speech: Emphasized that family planning is not just a health intervention but a key driver of economic growth, stating that savings from family planning initiatives could be redirected to infrastructure, education, and healthcare.

a7341.speaker: Ms. Daju Kachollom Shangti, Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
a7341.speech: Declaring the conference open on behalf of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, reaffirmed the government's commitment to strengthening family planning programs nationwide.

a7341.speaker: Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS)
a7341.speech: According to the NDHS, the average age of sexual debut in Nigeria is 15 years.

a7341.speaker: Association for the Advancement of Family Planning (AAFP), in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
a7341.speech: Pledged to track progress on these commitments and engage policymakers to ensure implementation.

a7368.speaker: Chief Medical Directors (CMDs) of University Teaching Hospitals and Federal Medical Centres (FMCs)
a7368.speech: "Our hospitals will be empty in the next one or two years." That was the alarming warning from the CMDs while defending the 2025 budget before the House of Representatives Committee on Health Institutions last week.

a7368.speaker: Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7368.speech: Revealed that Nigeria had only 55,000 licensed doctors and as many as 300,000 health professionals across various cadres to cater to the country's growing population of over 220 million; further disclosed that the country had lost about 16,000 doctors to foreign migration in the past five years; and said the brain drain, popularly referred to as the 'japa syndrome,' has significantly impacted the country's health sector by depriving Nigeria of its most skilled professionals.

a7368.speaker: Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7368.speech: In 2024 made it clear that while the government cannot restrict freedom of movement, efforts will be made to create a more favourable environment to encourage health workers to stay and practice in Nigeria: "We're not stopping anyone from leaving. We're accepting that migration is here to stay. People will leave, some will come back, and some will migrate here from elsewhere."

a7368.speaker: Daily Trust (editorial)
a7368.speech: "We at Daily Trust call for a state of emergency to be declared in the healthcare sector." The Nigerian government must invest not only in infrastructure but also in the welfare of medical staff by offering competitive salaries, better working conditions, and ensuring the safety and well-being of medical personnel; called on the federal government to take immediate action as the consequences of a failing and collapsing health sector are too grave to ignore.
